archetype: An aristocrats sacrifice engine that kills by drain, not by combat. strategic_frame.json declares 'combo' and the artifacts agree: five tutors, four declared kill lines, thirteen checker-passed stacks. The 28 creatures read as an aggro count only because in this deck the fodder IS the combo. COUNTING CONVENTION, held on every axis below: every figure is deck-audit's, taken over all 100 copies — the 99 plus Yawgmoth. Where the audit credits him it names him in the card list (interaction); where it does not (protection, card-advantage) it files him under possible_uncounted and I do not add him back in.
verdict: This deck functions and it converts. Mana is at every target, the turn-3 land drop lands 91.9% of the time, and nine drain payoffs sit behind four independently verified kills. What limits it is not speed and not card flow — it is that the 99 cannot answer an opposing artifact at all, while three of those four kills run on graveyard recursion — the thing the format's cheap artifact hosers are printed to attack. Whether a specific one stops them is routed to resolve-stack below, not assumed here. Interaction-breadth is the axis that binds; sweepers is the only axis the audit's target field marks over budget, and that target quotes a fragment — the corpus's current window is 3–4, so four is at the top of it rather than past it.

cut_candidates.why: The 99 holds exactly four removal:spot spells — Deadly Rollick, Fatal Push, Feed the Swarm, Snuff Out (role scan over all 79 entries) — and every one of them answers a creature. Only Feed the Swarm ('destroy target creature or enchantment an opponent controls') reaches a second class. So the whole spot-removal budget is depth on the one class already covered, while artifact and land have nothing. Snuff Out is the one to take out of that four, and NOT because it is the narrowest: Fatal Push's 'mana value 2 or less' gate binds at least as often as 'nonblack', and in a deck that sacrifices a creature most turns its revolt clause is usually live at 4. It goes because the other three each do something it cannot — Deadly Rollick exiles rather than destroys and is also free, Fatal Push costs one mana, and Feed the Swarm is the only card in the 99 answering an enchantment. One figure this entry no longer uses: interaction-breadth's creature count of 16 is text proximity, not answers. I read all sixteen — Animate Dead matches on 'Enchanted creature gets -1/-0' (its own reanimated body), Yahenni and Blasting Station on their 'Sacrifice a creature' activation costs, Sinister Gnarlbark on blight, which puts the counter on a creature you control. The clean depth figure is axes[6]'s thirteen.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: One of only two spells in the 99 with an alternative cost that lets it be cast for no mana (Deadly Rollick is the other), so it is an answer you can hold up on a turn your mana is already committed to a loop. Losing it makes Deadly Rollick the only free answer, and Deadly Rollick's alternative cost requires you to control a commander — the exact situation in which you have already been attacked.

open_questions.question: Under Grafdigger's Cage, do KILL A (stack 009), KILL B (stack 011) and KILL D (stack 010) still function? A and B recast Gravecrawler from the graveyard; D returns a creature card from the graveyard to the battlefield via undying. KILL C (stack 012) involves no graveyard. No checker has settled the Cage reading for this deck, and the 99 has no answer to an artifact.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If the reading is that Cage stops them, the artifact hole is not a breadth statistic — it is one two-mana card that switches off three of four declared kills with no recourse. That would justify a second artifact answer beyond Gate to Phyrexia; the current prescription is deliberately sized for the measured axis alone, not for this reading.

open_questions.question: Under an opposing Cursed Totem, what survives of the sacrifice-outlet component? Five of its eight members are creatures with activated abilities (Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Woe Strider, Yahenni, Warren Soultrader) and three are artifacts (Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Blasting Station); the commander is a sixth creature-activated outlet.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The outlet component's 77.9% is the number the whole engine's redundancy argument rests on. If a single artifact takes it to three cards, the component is not redundant against the decks that matter, and it is the same artifact-removal purchase that answers it.

open_questions.question: How often does this deck assemble ANY of its four kills? The audit reports 1.1%, 0.5%, 6.9% and 4.6% unassisted, and states that its schema cannot express the union of independent kills.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those four figures cannot be summed and averaging them would invent a number. The union is the actual conversion rate of the deck, and nothing in the repo currently reports it — which means nobody can say whether four kill lines are converting or merely present.

open_questions.question: Is the RENEWABLE FODDER component's seven-card count measuring one function? Its members are Nest of Scarabs, Bitterblossom, Grave Titan, Sedgemoor Witch, Black Market Connections, Reassembling Skeleton and Gravecrawler. Reading all seven: two — Bitterblossom and Black Market Connections — make a body on your own turn cycle with no board state and no mana. The other five each need something first: Nest of Scarabs a -1/-1 counter placed, Sedgemoor Witch an instant or sorcery cast, Grave Titan an entry or a combat step, and Reassembling Skeleton ({1}{B}) and Gravecrawler ({B}, plus a Zombie) mana per body.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is why Ophiomancer is NOT prescribed here, and the previous iteration of this document was wrong to prescribe it. Ranked by the audit's standalone prices the components run payoff 0.824, outlet 0.779, renewable fodder 0.736, ignition 0.731, engine mana 0.619, tutors 0.606, fast mana 0.427 — renewable fodder is the third-healthiest of the seven, and buying it with the list's only painful cut is a trade the measurement does not support. deck_recon.json (as_of 2026-08-03) records Ophiomancer at 73.5% of 6,961 Yawgmoth lists and 82.96% of the 446 combo-tagged subset and calls fodder 'this deck's measured bottleneck'; the audit contradicts that bottleneck claim outright, and recon is evidence, not authority. Those percentages are perishable and were not re-fetched. If re-declaring the component as mana-free renewable fodder only takes it to two cards, its real rate is far below 0.736 and Ophiomancer becomes the cheapest closer — four triggers a turn cycle, at the cost that it is a Human, so Mikaeus cannot grant it undying and it cannot serve as KILL D's non-Human body.

findings.note: Ordering re-derived independently from goldfish_targets.json (declared any_of sizes) joined to goldfish_metrics.json assembled_rate, not taken from the doctor. goldfish_targets holds 14 targets: 4 multi-component KILL targets (0.005/0.011/0.046/0.069) and 10 single-component targets whose assembled_rate IS that component's drawn rate. Those 10 ascending: Gravecrawler 0.165 (1), Bastion of Remembrance 0.167 (1), Feed the Swarm 0.173 (1), fast mana 0.427 (3), tutors 0.606 (5), engine mana 0.619 (5), ignition 0.731 (8), fodder 0.736 (7), outlet 0.779 (8), drain 0.824 (9) — byte-for-byte the doctor's list. Restricting to the seven MULTI-CARD ones leaves sizes 3,5,5,7,8,8,9 and rates 0.427-0.824: fast mana is uniquely smallest AND uniquely lowest, no tie on either. The qualifier 'the audit prices on their own' is also exactly right — it excludes the components nested inside the four KILL targets, which the audit never prices standalone. Claim true as re-scoped.

Same ordering verified as above. The 'concentration, not redundancy' distinction is sound, not rhetorical, on three independent grounds. (1) The audit's own notes block makes it first: '7 declared target(s) rest on a component with one card. A named card is 7.1% of an opening seven; that is the ceiling on those lines, NOT A DEFECT in the simulation.' (2) The three one-card rates cluster at 0.165/0.167/0.173 — that spread is the structural floor for drawing any one named card, so those numbers carry no information about redundancy and cannot be ranked against a 3-card class. (3) strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors, read whole, is built on exactly this split: 'a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven' versus an 'effect-class' that climbs with copies. Ranking a named card against an effect class is the error the cited section exists to prevent. I specifically attacked 'only one of them is buyable with a card' against this document's own single_points_of_failure[1].closers = [Nether Traitor, Forsaken Miner] for Gravecrawler, which looks contradictory. It resolves on oracle text: Nether Traitor returns only 'whenever ANOTHER creature is put into your graveyard from the battlefield', so sacrificing it does not return it and it cannot self-loop off a sac outlet; Forsaken Miner returns on committing a crime (targeting an opponent), which sacrificing your own creature is not. Neither substitutes into KILL A/B, where Gravecrawler is CAST from the graveyard off Warren Soultrader (a Zombie) paying with Soultrader's own Treasure — so neither would raise the 0.165 without a new stack. Bastion's redundancy (Zulaport Cutthroat, Blood Artist) is already in the 99 and already priced in the 9-card drain component at 0.824, so no ADD raises it either. The claim is true; closers and buyability are different questions and both fields are correct.

Confirmed unchanged AND correct, which is stronger than untouched. count=3 and len(have)=3 (['Sol Ring','Ancient Tomb','Dark Ritual']) matches goldfish_targets.json's any_of for 'Fast mana drawn' exactly; measured_rate=0.427 matches that target's assembled_rate in goldfish_metrics.json exactly; thinnest=false is right because the diagnosis uses global-minimum semantics and the sole thinnest=true is components[8] (Gravecrawler, 0.165), the true global minimum. I cross-checked all ten components this way, not just this one: every count equals its declared any_of size and every measured_rate equals its metrics assembled_rate, with zero mismatches.

Grave Pact is a genuine painful cut and the document stands on its own for its unpaired status. The cost is real and independent of 'why', not a restatement: I verified against data/card_roles.json that Grave Pact is the ONLY card in the 99 carrying removal:edict (the whole deck yields exactly ['Grave Pact']), so 'the only removal:edict' is literally true, and the entry argues AGAINST its own cut ('against a creature deck going wider than thirteen removal spells it is the best card in the list'). orphans_stack: [] is correct — no file in stacks/ mentions Grave Pact at all, and it appears in none of the four declared kill lines.
